item.title: HAX Lab
item.content:
HAX Lab is where students and junior developers learn web development by shipping real work in HAX, the open source web publishing platform built at Penn State. Interns spend a term in the College of Arts and Architecture, and each one owns one real project: a theme, the command line, the design system, the dashboard. What they build ships to everyone who uses HAX.

Find your way in

New to web development? Go from nothing to your first HAX contribution, one page at a time.

Class, clubs, the lab, faculty grants and industry, and how to join.

The Sustainable Impact and Innovation Pipeline: how a course becomes a contributor pipeline.

Everyone the lab credits, and where they landed.

Faculty who have secured funding for lab work, and how to bring the lab a problem.

What the lab built for HAX, and what it did for the students.

HAX Lab in the HAX network

The lab is one stop in a network of HAX sites. You'll use all of them in onboarding.

  • HAXTheWeb: what HAX is for and every way to get it.
  • PRAW (hax.cloud): the stories behind the lab and the people in it.
  • Build now: make a HAX site in your browser tab, nothing to install.
  • Learn: tutorials for using HAX one flow at a time.
  • Web components: every HAX element with a live demo, including ones lab students built.
  • The issue queue: work tagged for the lab.

Talk to us

Want to intern, send a class, or bring the lab a problem? Contact Product Owner Bill Rose or Project Lead Bryan Ollendyke.
